lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Algorithms.StoppingPower:QuantumComputation.Specs.ApproximatesTimeEvolution
lean.annotation: The projector in `ApproximatesTimeEvolution` restricts the input, not the output: the joint norm charges both error within the valid-grid, zero-workspace subspace and amplitude outside it. For an allowed normalized input, the probability of observing an invalid momentum encoding or any nonzero ancilla is therefore at most $(10^{-2})^2=10^{-4}$ in total, not necessarily zero.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.fermionicProjector
lean.annotation: For a fixed `spinUp` subset of size $s$, `fermionicProjector` averages electron permutations that preserve that subset and its complement, weighting each by its sign and dividing by $s!(218-s)!$. A matrix entry is zero if either index is invalid; otherwise only permutations matching the two electron momentum assignments contribute, and the projectile momenta must agree.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPowerSolution.ComposableLiveEndpoint.gqsp_hTotErr11
lean.plain: Total error at most 10⁻² for each evolution time
lean.annotation: For each of the ten evolution times, `gqsp_hTotErr11` checks a one-run budget: the segment count times the per-segment error bound `nSeg j / 2^48`, twice the phase-gradient preparation error, and time times the Hamiltonian error cap. The preparation charge is not multiplied by the segment count, and the energy cap in Hartrees contributes a dimensionless error after multiplication by time in atomic units.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPowerSolution.FermionicKrylovSegBridge.stepa_perturbation_via_fermProjector_gen
lean.plain: Why a Hamiltonian bound on the fermionic sector suffices
lean.annotation: The perturbation bridge restricts the grid error to the fermionic sector using GP = PG = P. Under its Hermiticity, sector-commutation, and error-budget hypotheses, it absorbs the scalar shift into the phase and adds at most t(δ_prep + ε_id) ≤ t ε_BE to the evolution error for the conjugated Hamiltonian in the working encoding.

lean.name: RealizesUnitaryFromBasisOutcomesAndZeroWorkspace
lean.plain: Unitary realization on selected basis inputs
lean.annotation: `restrictToBasisOutcomes` and `restrictToZeroAncilla` independently select the valid system span and zero workspace at input. The realization predicate compares the circuit with the joint unitary $W$ on those inputs without imposing exact zero workspace at output; the separate evolution bound controls output error on physical inputs.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.stoppingPower_correctness

lean.annotation: For each allowed configuration, time $t=j+1$ a.u., and disjoint register placement, the compiled circuit exactly realizes one joint unitary $W$ on the span of valid grid inputs with zero ancillas. The same $W$ meets the $10^{-2}$ evolution bound on every same-spin antisymmetric sector, with one phase for all inputs within each sector but no requirement that the phase be shared across sectors.

lean.name: QuantumComputationDiscoveries.Algorithms.StoppingPower:QuantumComputation.Specs.ApproximatesTimeEvolution
lean.annotation: The factor `input` on the right projects onto the selected spin sector and the all-zero ancilla state. The operator norm of the restricted difference is the largest vector error over unit inputs in that subspace. The output vector includes the ancillas, so the bound also controls any component with nonzero output ancillas.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.StoppingPower.fermionicProjector
lean.annotation: Multiplying `fermionicProjector` by a same-spin exchange reindexes the signed permutation sum and reverses every sign. A vector in the range therefore changes sign under that exchange. Applying the same one-electron basis change to all electron registers commutes with the exchanges, so the antisymmetry condition persists in the position basis.

lean.annotation: For each joint output observable $M$, Lean compares the program's weakest precondition with $W^\dagger M W$. It applies the same input projector to both expressions, then requires the program's expression to be at least as large in the positive-semidefinite order. The quantifier includes observables with off-diagonal entries, so the statement checks coherence between valid momentum configurations as well as their outcome probabilities.
